title: What Saudi Arabia Really Gave Ronaldo
on_screen_hook: WHAT DID SAUDI REALLY GIVE HIM?

story_spine.character: Cristiano Ronaldo, a forward of thirty-seven with no club when this starts, who cries in a dugout at thirty-nine and with a trophy at forty-one
story_spine.question: What did Saudi Arabia really do for him, and what did he do for Saudi Arabia?
story_spine.driving_question: So what did Saudi Arabia really do for him, and what did he do for Saudi Arabia?
story_spine.cold_open: 3 Jan 2023: he sits at the press table in Riyadh and says South Africa. It gains meaning at the last line, which returns to that table: this first ordinary, human moment is where every later claim about what the kingdom did for him began.
scenes: Nov 2022 to Jan 2023: Morgan, United exit, Morocco; Al-Muammar's account of who moved first; the fireworks at Mrsool Park
Jan to Feb 2023: the cohabitation question and 'bent the laws' posts; first money reports; the Four Seasons; debut and Founding Day
Jan 2023 to Feb 2024: followers and the record spend; the 99 lashes rumour; a real ban
May 2024: thirty-five goals, then King's Cup tears, four days apart
May to Dec 2025: 'this chapter is over', the extension and every pay figure; our maths; tourism, White House, Amnesty, villas, the beach claim
May to Oct 2026: the title, 985 goals, deal to June 2027, sale talks
The answer: back to the law question; then the wedding in Portugal
story_spine.thesis: The record shows a trade of money for attention, not a kingdom rewriting its law for one man.
story_spine.payoff: He did marry her, in Portugal; Saudi Arabia gave him the money, he gave it attention, and no record shows a law rewritten for him.
story_spine.loop_line: And no record shows a law rewritten for the man who once sat at that press table.

beats.narration: Cristiano Ronaldo sat at a press table in Riyadh and told the world he'd come to South Africa.
beats.on_screen: Hook text: WHAT DID SAUDI REALLY GIVE HIM?
beats.visual_intent: 15_south_africa_slip.mp4, segment 12.0-17.5: the slip itself on frame 1.

beats.narration: He'd just signed for Al-Nassr, on a contract that has never been *published*.
beats.on_screen: Label: 3 Jan 2023, Riyadh. Small line: REPORTED FIGURES ONLY, CONTRACT NEVER PUBLISHED. Optional text: South African Tourism replied it was 'patiently waiting' (SBS).

beats.narration: The internet filled that silence with pay figures, a closed beach, even a rewritten law.
beats.visual_intent: Fast teaser: 71_card_table_pay_by_season.png, 80_card_claim_beach.png, 79_card_claim_law_changed.png (top halves only, verdicts cropped so the answer stays withheld).

beats.narration: So what did Saudi Arabia really do for him, and what did he do for Saudi Arabia?
Two months earlier he'd told Piers Morgan he felt betrayed by Manchester United. His contract ended, and after the World Cup he was thirty-seven with no club.
beats.on_screen: Label: Nov-Dec 2022

beats.narration: So who approached first? The only first-hand account is from Al-Nassr's president then, Musalli Al-Muammar, three years later.
beats.on_screen: 77_card_timeline_joining.png. Line: AL-MUAMMAR'S ACCOUNT ONLY, VIA SUMMARIES.

beats.narration: He said a Saudi prince proposed it in July twenty twenty-two, and that contact through a family member led to Lisbon and the sports minister.
beats.on_screen: Card 77, July 2022 row. Mendes vs Regufe dispute stays off the voice; put on screen if room.

beats.narration: We found nothing from Ronaldo confirming that. And Saudi's state wealth fund didn't control the club until the following June.
beats.on_screen: On screen: PIF 75%, 5 June 2023. No source gives PIF a role in the 2022 approach.

beats.narration: On December thirtieth Al-Nassr announced him, no transfer fee reported. Four days later he came through the fireworks at a sold-out Mrsool Park.
beats.on_screen: Label: Mrsool Park, Riyadh. 25,000 capacity per The National.

beats.narration: He arrived with Georgina Rodriguez, both foreigners, unmarried, in a country where reports said living together outside marriage was forbidden.
beats.on_screen: On screen: reports cite no statute.
beats.visual_intent: 12_arrival_georgina_flowers.jpg, 27_riyadh_skyline_dusk.jpg. Adults only in frame; no framing on the children.

beats.narration: Headlines soon said special permission. One post quoted in Newsweek said he made them bend their laws instead of just marrying her.
beats.on_screen: Pull-quote: 'He made them bend their laws instead of just marrying her.' X user, via Newsweek, Jan 2023.

beats.narration: Hold on to that one.
On the money, CBS had reported about seventy-five million dollars a year in basic salary.
beats.on_screen: 72_card_compare_original_deal_2022.png, top. Tag REPORTED.

beats.narration: Other reports put the full package around two hundred million euros a year, with commercial deals, and the split was never published.
beats.on_screen: Card 72 lower half, then 85_card_quote_no_world_cup_clause.png.

beats.narration: Home was a Four Seasons suite in Kingdom Tower, reported at two hundred fifty to three hundred thousand dollars a month.
beats.on_screen: 84_card_list_where_he_lives.png, top. No hotel price published.

beats.narration: One later report says a villa in Al-Muhammadiyah, but we couldn't confirm where he lives now.
beats.on_screen: Card 84 bottom line.
beats.visual_intent: 32_diplomatic_quarter_drive.mp4 seg 84-91 as generic Riyadh, never implied as his home.

beats.narration: By January tenth, the club's Instagram was up more than a thousand percent, to about eleven million.
beats.on_screen: 87_card_list_what_saudi_got.png, first rows (also 57.5m all platforms).

beats.narration: He debuted as captain that January, and within three weeks scored all four in a four-nil.
beats.on_screen: Label: Debut, 22 Jan 2023. First goal 3 Feb, four v Al-Wehda 9 Feb on screen.

beats.narration: That summer Saudi clubs spent a record nine hundred fifty-seven million dollars, though his part in it is argued.
beats.on_screen: Card 87, third row (Deloitte). Benzema, Neymar on screen.

beats.narration: The rumours grew with him. One had Iran sentencing him to ninety-nine lashes, until Iran's embassy in Spain denied any ruling.
beats.on_screen: 81_card_claim_99_lashes.png, then 82_card_claim_conversion.png (conversion and sujood stay on screen; no sujood clip exists).

beats.narration: Saudi rules did reach him. In February twenty twenty-four, a gesture at fans chanting Messi cost him a one-match ban.
beats.on_screen: On screen: SAR 10,000 fine, non-appealable, via Al Jazeera.
beats.visual_intent: 50_al_shabab_feb2024_match_official.mp4 (the gesture itself isn't in the listed segments).

beats.narration: He kept scoring, thirty-five league goals by May twenty-seventh, a Saudi record.
beats.on_screen: 78_card_timeline_football.png row. Guinness.

beats.narration: Four days later, the King's Cup final in Jeddah went to penalties. He scored his. Al-Nassr lost.
beats.on_screen: Label: King's Cup final, 31 May 2024.

beats.narration: He sat in the dugout in *tears* while staff tried to comfort him.
Forbes, which only estimates, put his football income at two hundred million dollars for that season, then two hundred twenty-five million for the next.
beats.on_screen: 71_card_table_pay_by_season.png rows, 76_card_chart_forbes_on_off_field.png. Forbes windows differ from seasons.

beats.narration: In May twenty twenty-five he posted that this chapter was over. A month later he signed for two more years.
beats.on_screen: Labels: 26 May, 26 June 2025.

beats.narration: The Sun, from unnamed sources, printed a hundred seventy-eight million pounds a year plus a signing bonus, one tabloid, unconfirmed, and the only figure for this season.
beats.on_screen: 73_card_list_extension_the_sun.png; card 71 row 2026/27.

beats.narration: Forbes estimated two hundred thirty-five million dollars for the year to May twenty twenty-six.
beats.on_screen: 74_card_breakdown_forbes_division.png top half: ESTIMATE.

beats.narration: Our own maths on that *estimate* gives nineteen and a half million a month, four and a half million a week, about six hundred forty-four thousand dollars a day.
beats.on_screen: Card 74 rows, OUR DIVISION tag always visible.
beats.visual_intent: Card 74, row by row on the words.

beats.narration: A per-match fee? None has been reported. Divide by his thirty-seven games that season and it's about six point three five million dollars a game, our arithmetic, not his contract.
beats.on_screen: 75_card_table_per_match.png: NO APPEARANCE FEE HAS BEEN REPORTED. Stake: 83_card_claim_stake.png, reports only, on screen.

beats.narration: Saudi Arabia got his face on a tourism campaign. That November he sat at the White House dinner for its Crown Prince, and in Riyadh said he considered himself Saudi.
beats.on_screen: Source line: Visit Saudi, Sept 2025. Pull-quote: 'I consider myself Saudi', TOURISE, Nov 2025.

beats.narration: Amnesty International had said from the start that his signing fit a pattern of sportswashing.
beats.on_screen: Amnesty attributed; 81 executed in one day in 2022, per Amnesty. Card 87 lower row.

beats.narration: That December he and Georgina bought two villas on a Red Sea island, reached by boat or seaplane.
beats.on_screen: Card 84 Nujuma row; price is The Sun's, screen only.

beats.narration: The viral story goes further, a whole Saudi beach closed for a day for his family.
beats.on_screen: 80_card_claim_beach.png claim line.

beats.narration: We searched in English and Arabic and couldn't confirm it, or trace where it began. We can't disprove it either.
beats.on_screen: Card 80: UNVERIFIED; nearest is the unconfirmed Riyadh park closure.

beats.narration: In May twenty twenty-six, five days after losing an Asian final, he scored twice against Damac and won the league, at forty-one, in tears again.
beats.on_screen: Label: 21 May 2026, 4-1 v Damac.

beats.narration: He has about nine hundred eighty-five goals now. His deal ends in June twenty twenty-seven, he told Vogue this is probably his last year, and RedBird confirmed early interest in the club, no deal yet.
beats.on_screen: 86_card_stat_goals_985.png. On screen: A Bola consortium report, PIF reportedly 100%.

beats.narration: So, did Saudi Arabia change its law for him?
beats.visual_intent: Near-still on 28_riyadh_night_from_iss.jpg; riser ends on the reveal cut.

beats.narration: The truth was, nobody has shown that it did. We found no *decree*, no regulation, no official statement either way. The story traces to two anonymous lawyers, who told the agency EFE the ban still stood but authorities had stopped interfering with foreigners generally. The hotel rule people cite dates from twenty nineteen, and British advice still calls sex outside marriage illegal. So what's on record is a blind eye described for foreigners, not a law bent for one man.
beats.on_screen: Card 79_card_claim_law_changed.png: NO EVIDENCE (sound-off match). Sources: EFE via Bio Bio; Al Jazeera 2019; UK FCDO. No statute named.
beats.visual_intent: Card 79, row by row on the words.

beats.narration: And he did marry her. They lived together unmarried until August eleventh, twenty twenty-six, then wed in a civil ceremony in Cascais, in Portugal, not Saudi Arabia. So here's the honest answer. Saudi Arabia gave him the money, whatever the real figure is, since nobody has published the contract, and he gave it the world's attention. And no record shows a law rewritten for the man who once sat at that press table.
beats.on_screen: Name card during the line: CRISTIANO RONALDO. Small line: pay figures are estimates.
beats.visual_intent: 58_wedding_bands_hands.jpg, 63_cascais_estoril_bay.jpg, then 15_south_africa_slip.mp4 lead-in so the loop lands on b01.

publish.title: What Saudi Arabia Really Gave Ronaldo
publish.description: How Cristiano Ronaldo went from Manchester United to Riyadh, what was reported about his pay, and what the record actually shows on the claims about Saudi law and a closed beach. All pay here is estimated: his contract has never been published, and every per-month, per-day and per-game figure is our own division of a press estimate. A documentary on a living person, built from sourced reports.
publish.comment_prompt: If the contract were published tomorrow, which number do you think would turn out closest: Forbes or The Sun?
publish.pinned_comment: Sources: CBS, AFP via GOAL, Forbes via Wikipedia, The Sun via GOAL/SI, EFE via Bio Bio, Al Jazeera 2019, UK FCDO, Newsweek, Amnesty, ESPN, AP, UPI. Pay is estimated; contract unpublished; divisions are ours. Beach claim could not be confirmed or traced. Which is closest, Forbes or The Sun?
